newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada hopes to privatize nuclear research lab.
newsitem.headline: Canada hopes to privatize nuclear research lab.

text.p: The Canadian government hopes to complete plans to privatize one of Atomic Energy of Canada Limited's (AECL) flagship research laboratories by the end of June, government officials said on Thursday.
The future of the Whiteshell Laboratories in Pinawa, Manitoba, has been uncertain for the last two years, but it appeared that either a Canadian or a British firm may be poised to take it over.

The laboratory, which employs nearly 700 people, conducts research into nuclear reactor safety and nuclear waste management. It also produces medical radioisotopes used in cancer diagnosis and treatment.
Layoffs at the government-owned laboratories were to have begun on March 31 but were delayed until June 30, in the hope that a new owner/operator would be found.

Natural Resources Assistant Deputy Minister Mike Cleland, said the layoffs were delayed to ensure that the sites remain attractive to a new owner. "Part of the attractiveness of the site is definitely the people associated with it," he said.
Government officials said the hoped to make an announcement within weeks regarding the Whiteshell facility.
The Winnipeg Free Press reported on Thursday that a bid by a consortium led by British Nuclear Fuels PLC to take over Whiteshell had been selected over a rival bid from Golder Group of Toronto.
Pierre Gratton, a spokesman for Natural Resouces Minister Anne McLellan, would not confirm the report.

"We've received two very serious bids each with pros and cons and they are being looked at now," he said. "Nothing has been submitted to ministers for recommendation (and) ministers have not made a decision."

AECL intended to close the laboratories after the Canadian government announced C$100 million in cuts to the agency's funding. A government-appointed task force reviewed the decision and suggested the facility could be privatized.
